facts.fact: The Republic of the Congo, representing Central Africa, was elected Rapporteur of the bureau of the African Union Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and ICT at its 5th Ordinary Session in November 2023, and still serves in that office per the 2026 notice.

facts.fact: The Seventh ATU Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja elected the Republic of the Congo to the 25-member Administrative Council of the African Telecommunications Union for the next four-year period; the Congo also put forward a Secretary-General candidate and withdrew him after the third round.

The African Telecommunications Union's own release says the Seventh Conference of Plenipotentiaries in Abuja elected the Republic of the Congo, for Central Africa, to the 25-member Administrative Council for the next four years; the Congo withdrew its Secretary-General candidate after the third round.

note: The SADX pilot is in Benin, Ghana and Rwanda and the agreement is with a company; the Congo is not named.

facts.fact: A two-day regional workshop on a common framework for national emergency telecommunications plans opened in Brazzaville on 15 September 2026, convened by the ITU, the Assembly of Central Africa telecom regulators (ARTAC) and Congo's ARPCE, with eight ECCAS states taking part.

facts.fact: Congo's media regulator CSLC and DR Congo's CSAC signed a memorandum of understanding in Kinshasa at the close of talks on 19-20 August 2026, covering technical cooperation on regulating media and digital platforms and joint action on disinformation; the signing day is not given, so the last day of talks is used.

note: Opening of a bilateral media-regulators round table; cooperation agreed in words, no instrument signed and no African digital-policy body involved.

facts.fact: Congo's regulator says it signed a free-roaming MoU with Gabon in October 2019 and joined the collegial signature of CEMAC bilateral MoUs in November 2021.
The Congo regulator reports free roaming with Gabon in effect, with call volumes shown before and after its start.
The Congo regulator publishes Congo-Gabon roaming call counts from January 2020 to December 2024, for example 81,563 in December 2024.
ARCEP Gabon says Gabon and Congo signed roaming protocols, with SMS and data added in 2021.
ARCEP Gabon says free roaming with Congo went into service for voice on 15 October 2019 and was extended to SMS and data.
